title: South Korea Hosted API: Localization & Launch Playbook
body:
Purpose:
A compact playbook for shipping the South Korea-hosted Redwood API offering (initial beta). Focus: low-latency hosted endpoints in Seoul region, Korean language quality signals, localized terms/policy, and channel enablement for early enterprise & platform partners.

Executive positioning (one-liner):
Redwood Hosted Korea: enterprise-grade inference closer to your users — predictable latency, Korean-first model evaluations, and flexible enterprise controls for regulated data.

Target segments (priority):
- Fintech platforms requiring sub-50ms token latency for chatbots and risk workflows (enterprise sales target).
- Consumer apps (messaging, search) wanting local embeddings and semantic search with regional endpoints.
- ISVs & platform partners (Naver Cloud / KT integrations) seeking joint go-to-market.

Key differentiators to highlight in messaging:
- Regional latency SLAs + multi-az Seoul availability for deterministic response times.
- Korean language eval suite results (release note: 92% pass on intent-preservation for top-10 prompts).
- Unified API: same SDKs and rollouts as global hosted API — easy migration between regions.
- Enterprise-grade controls: VPC peering, configurable token retention, KMS integrations.
- Cost-performance controls: recommended batching and quant profiles for Hangul-heavy workloads.

Competitive notes (quick sketch):
- OpenAI / Global LLM APIs: strong general brand, but single-region + cross-border latency; positioning = "local latency & enterprise controls".
- Naver/Hyundai/Korean cloud ML: native language strengths, incumbency on data regulation; position on interoperability and standardized API (we run curated open models and offer predictable SLOs).
- Local ML startups: may offer bespoke models; differentiate with platform reliability, rollout tooling, and multi-environment parity (hosted -> dedicated -> private).

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: Korean regulatory and data residency questions from enterprise legal teams.
  Mitigation: Provide short legal FAQ + sample DPA addendum; offer Private deployment option for high-regulation customers.
- Risk: Perceived model quality vs local players.
  Mitigation: Publish side-by-side evals on representative KR prompts; include customer pilot results.
- Risk: Early capacity bottlenecks during beta.
  Mitigation: Staggered beta invites, partner commitments for reserved capacity, transparent fallback to global endpoints.

Launch assets to prepare (owner initials):
- Beta page + signup form (GTM): Maya L.
- One-pager: localized KR copy + English variant (Marcom): Jae H. P.
- Press/partner announcement draft (for partners): PR draft + partner brief: Ethan M.
- Sales cheat sheet (objections + pricing guide): GTM sales enablement: Priya S.
- Technical FAQ & runbook for SRE/Support: Sook-hee C.
- Korean-language eval report (appendix): Applied ML: Jae H. P.

Suggested messaging snippets (adaptable):
- Email subject (enterprise): "Lower latency for KR users — Redwood Hosted API in Seoul (Private beta)"
- Press headline draft: "Redwood Inference launches Seoul-hosted API for faster, compliant Korean-language inference"
- Sales opener: "Same Redwood API, now in Korea — faster responses, enterprise controls, and local support to accelerate your AI features."

Pricing & packaging notes (beta):
- Beta pricing: introductory 20% off hosted rates for first 6 months for committed pilots.
- Dedicated footprint for enterprise pilots: quote-based (min commit).
- Notes: display approximate token unit economics with Korea infra premium callout.

Partner outreach plan (initial):
- Priority: Naver Cloud (market access & co-marketing), KT (connectivity + telco SI), local system integrators focused on finance/health.
- Tactics: partner pilot documents, joint webinars, regional meetup sponsorships.

Enablement checklist (practical ops items):
- [ ] Localized developer docs and quickstart (KR translations) — DOCS-1193 — owner: Docs squad
- [ ] SDK region option flags + sample configs for seoul region — ENG-5432 — owner: SDK team
- [ ] GA readiness checklist for latency SLO reporting and alerting in Console — OBS-2701 — owner: Observability
- [ ] Sales playbook + objection handling + pricing worksheets — GTM-912 — owner: GTM
- [ ] Legal DPA template with KR residency appendix — LEGAL-330 — owner: Legal
- [ ] Support routing: Seoul oncall + Korean-language triage docs — SRE-730 — owner: SRE

Sample internal announcement (Slack / All-hands snippet):
"Heads-up: We're opening a Seoul-hosted beta for Redwood Hosted API next month. Core benefits: lower latency for KR users, enterprise privacy controls, and partner integrations with Naver Cloud. Kickoff Q&A and pilot signups will be handled through the GTM channel — please route partner intros to @Priya. More details: confluence link above."

Customer-facing FAQ (short):
Q: Why host in Seoul?
A: To reduce cross-region latency, meet customer data-residency preferences, and offer localized support and billing in the APAC time zone.
Q: Is model quality different?
A: No — we run the same curated model catalog and publish localized eval results; you can pin versions and roll back like anywhere else.
Q: Can I get Private deployment?
A: Yes. Customers with strict compliance needs can choose Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) — contact sales for an architecture review.

Tactical timeline (quarter view):
- Week 0-2: finalize legal + pricing for beta; complete KR docs translations.
- Week 3-4: partner signups & pilot scoping; internal enablement sessions.
- Week 5: private beta soft-launch to 10 pilot customers.
- Week 6-10: iterate on latency configs, collect pilot feedback, publish KR eval report.
- Week 11-12: expand beta to GA candidates; finalize pricing.

Open questions (working notes):
- What telemetry + consent language do we need for local privacy regs? (legal)
- Do we want a Korean-language support rotation for GA or just pilot? (CS/SRE)
- Which local cloud partner(s) get early co-marketing vs technical onboarding priority? (GTM/Partnerships)

Appendix: Quick sample customer objection responses (sales):
- Objection: "We already use X local provider with Korean models."
  Reply: "Totally — many customers run hybrids. Redwood differentiates on consistent API, enterprise-grade SLAs, rollout tooling, and an explicit migration path between hosted/dedicated/private so you can standardize across teams."
- Objection: "What about latency under load?"
  Reply: "We publish per-route latency breakdowns in the Console and offer capacity commitments; for pilots we'll reserve capacity and run a low-latency test harness with you."

Notes to self (informal):
- prioritize legal Qs, partner intro deck, and a KR-specific eval artifact. get Sook-hee to review localization strings (particularly error copy).
- keep messaging tight: "local latency + enterprise controls" is the core.
